faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a child psychologist under the Health Professionals Award?
faqs.a: Under the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020, a child psychologist is typically classified as a Health Professional. Minimum rates vary by level: Level 6 is $32.09 per hour, Level 7 is $32.67, and Level 8 starts at $33.78. These rates apply to full-time employees working 38 ordinary hours per week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of these rates.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect a child psychologist's pay?

For a Level 6 child psychologist, the casual rate is $32.09 × 1.25 = $40.11 per hour. This loading compensates for entitlements casuals do not receive, such as paid leave. The loading is applied on top of the base rate, not included in it.

faqs.q: What is the estimated take-home pay for a child psychologist after tax and super?
faqs.a: For a full-time child psychologist earning the Level 6 rate of $32.09/hour (annual $63,420), the estimated take-home pay after 2026–27 tax (including Medicare levy) is about $49,300 per year, or $1,896 per fortnight. bodyMarkdown:
## Child Psychologist Salary: Understanding Award Rates and Your Pay

If you are researching a **child psychologist salary** in Australia, the starting point is the relevant award. Most child psychologists are covered by the **Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020**, which sets minimum pay rates for health professionals including psychologists. The award classifies employees into levels based on qualifications and experience. For example, a Level 6 Health Professional (often a psychologist with several years of experience) has a minimum hourly rate of **$32.09** as of July 2026. A Level 7 rate is **$32.67** per hour, and Level 8 starts at **$33.78**. These rates apply to full-time employees working 38 ordinary hours per week.

### How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Salary

To estimate an annual **child psychologist salary**, use the standard formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. We assume a full-time load of 38 hours per week, which is the ordinary hours under the award. For a Level 6 child psychologist at $32.09/hour, the calculation is:

- Weekly: $32.09 × 38 = **$1,219.42**
- Fortnightly: $1,219.42 × 2 = **$2,438.84**
- Annual: $1,219.42 × 52 = **$63,409.84** (rounded to $63,410)

This is the minimum annual salary before tax and super. Many child psychologists earn above the award rate, especially in private practice or with specialist qualifications. The [reference tables](/data) on this site provide further classification details.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

It is important to distinguish the **National Minimum Wage** from award rates. From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage is **$26.44 per hour** for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. This applies to award/agreement-free employees. However, child psychologists are almost always covered by the Health Professionals Award, which sets higher minimums. The award also includes a 25% casual loading for casual employees, bringing the casual rate for a Level 6 child psychologist to **$40.11 per hour**.

### Tax and Superannuation on a Child Psychologist Salary

When estimating take-home pay, you need to account for tax and super. The **Australian Taxation Office** 2026–27 resident tax rates are:
- $0–$18,200: nil
- $18,201–$45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001–$135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001–$190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- Above $190,000: 45%

Plus the **Medicare levy** of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners). For a $63,410 annual salary, the estimated tax and Medicare is around $14,100, leaving take-home pay of about **$49,300 per year** or **$1,896 per fortnight**. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised estimate.

**Superannuation** is paid on top of your salary by your employer. The **super guarantee** is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a $63,410 salary, super is $7,609.20 per year. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution to your super fund. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Casual Loading and Other Considerations

If you work as a casual child psychologist, you receive a 25% loading on the base hourly rate. For Level 6, that is $32.09 + 25% = **$40.11 per hour**. The loading compensates for not receiving paid leave, public holidays, or other entitlements. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to calculate it correctly. Never enter a rate that already includes loading into the calculator; always use the base rate and tick the casual checkbox.

### Comparing with Average Earnings

The **Australian Bureau of Statistics** reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were **$2,083.70** in May 2026 (about $108,352 annually). A child psychologist at the award minimum earns less than this average, but experienced psychologists or those in senior roles (Level 8 or 9) can earn closer to or above the average. For example, a Level 9 Health Professional (pay point 3) earns **$39.42 per hour**, or $77,869 annually. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides more context.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

To quickly convert any hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, or weekly figures, use [the timesheet](/) on this site. Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and select the casual checkbox if applicable. The calculator applies the 38-hour week, tax, and super automatically. Remember that the results are estimates; your actual pay may vary due to overtime, penalties, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

### Summary

A **child psychologist salary** under the Health Professionals Award starts at around $63,410 per year for a Level 6 full-time employee. With casual loading, the hourly rate rises to $40.11. After tax and Medicare, take-home pay is approximately $49,300, with super of $7,610 paid on top. Always check the latest award rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman and consult a tax professional for your specific situation.
